checks.label: The density of seawater is about 1025 kg/m³: the water takes ρgQH = 1025 × 9.81 × 0.0141 × 22, about 3.13 kW, with the valve open
The pressure at the bottom of the atmosphere is about (1025)(9.81)(10) Pa, about 10⁵ Pa: so 100 kPa holds up about 9.9 m of seawater
The intersection of both curves is the operating point: at every valve stop and speed that flows, the pump gives exactly the head the pipe needs
Closing a discharge valve changes the system resistance curve: each stop is steeper at every flow, so the flow falls and the head rises
At the no-flow condition, a shut valve, the pump builds its most head, and the power needed is at or near its least
As the flow rate increases, the motor's amperage rises: opening the valve stop by stop raises the flow and the shaft power together
The NPSH value is the minimum absolute pressure at the suction to avoid cavitation: the pump cavitates exactly when NPSH available falls below NPSH required
Every number the valve screens print comes from the rule: 14.1, 11.2, 8.5 and 5.6 L/s at 22.0, 25.0, 27.1 and 28.8 m, and 30.0 m shut; 4.41, 4.12, 3.85, 3.56 and 3.00 kW; 71, 68, 60 and 45%

The power and puzzle figures: 3.13 and 2.81 kW, with 2.8, 3.6 and 3.1 offered; 19.2 m, 9.6 L/s, 15.5 m and 2.15 kW at 80%; 9.1 m and no flow at 55%, 7.8 offered; 11.8 L/s at 24.4 m, or 18.7 without friction
Suction: NPSH available is about 10.6 m at +2 m, 5.6 m at −3 m and 4.6 m at −4 m, against 5.0 m required at 14.1 L/s, with 1.0 m of suction friction
The positive displacement pump gives 9.8 L/s at 15.8 m for 1.96 kW open, and 9.4 L/s at 62.7 m for 7.39 kW at friction ×10: its flow falls by under a twentieth while its head nearly quadruples
The efficiency hump peaks near 14 L/s at about 71%; by the pump laws, at 80% speed its peak is the same height at 80% of the flow
Each puzzle offers three different answers including its right one, every wrong answer has its own hint, and before Check nothing on its picture shows the answer or a warning mark
A wrong pick is drawn as a warning where it fails, and a right answer draws none
A right answer draws the rule's result: the flow climbs to 14.14 L/s; 11.18 L/s; 2.811 kW; no flow; 5.645 m available with no bubbles; 9.373 L/s; 8.452 L/s; 11.83 L/s
Every demonstration has finished within 4.5 s of its screen opening, its first move after the 0.35 s screen fade; every answer's motion, right or wrong, within 2 s
Every demonstration screen, with the live line under it, keeps to about 90 words
